title: IELTS Academic 19 - Listening Test 2 - Part 2
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 2

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

08:04ANNOUNCER: Part 2. You will hear a man called David talking on the radio about his work as a lifeboat volunteer.
08:13ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
09:03ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.
09:11DAVID: I never really planned to be a lifeboat volunteer when I came to live in Northsea. I'd been working in London as a website designer, but although that was interesting, I didn't like city life. I'd been really keen on boats as a teenager, and I thought if I went to live by the sea, I might be able to pursue that interest a bit more in my free time. Then I found that the Lifeboat Institution was looking for volunteers, so I decided to apply.
09:41DAVID: The Lifeboat Institution building here in Northsea is hard to miss, it's one of the largest in the country. It was built 15 years ago with funds provided by a generous member of the public who'd lived here all her life. As the Lifeboat Institution is a charity that relies on that kind of donation, rather than funding provided by the government, that was a huge help to us.
10:06DAVID: When I applied, I had to have a health assessment. The doctors were particularly interested in my vision. I used to be short-sighted, so I'd had to wear glasses, but I'd had laser eye surgery two years earlier so that was OK. They gave me tests for colour blindness and they thought I might have a problem there, but it turned out I was OK.
10:30DAVID: When the coastguard gets an alert, all the volunteers are contacted and rush to the lifeboat station. Our target's to get there in five minutes, then we try to get the boat off the dock and out to sea in another six to eight minutes. Our team's proud that we usually achieve that - the average time across the country's eight and a half minutes.
10:54DAVID: I've recently qualified as what's called a 'helmsman', which means I have the ultimate responsibility for the lifeboat. I have to check that the equipment we use is in working order - the crew have special life jackets that can support up to four people in the water. And it's ultimately my decision whether it's safe to launch the boat. But it's very rare not to launch it, even in the worst weather.
11:21DAVID: As well as going out on the lifeboat, my work involves other things too. A lot of people underestimate how quickly conditions can change at sea, so I speak to youth groups and sailing clubs in the area about the sorts of problems that sailors and swimmers can have if the weather suddenly gets bad. We also have a lot of volunteers who organise activities to raise money for us, and we couldn't manage without them.
11:53ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
12:19ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
12:26DAVID: The training we get is a continuous process, focusing on technical competence and safe handling techniques, and it's given me the confidence to deal with extreme situations without panicking. I was glad I'd done a first aid course before I started, as that's a big help with the casualty care activities we do. We've done a lot on how to deal with ropes and tie knots - that's an essential skill. After a year, I did a one-week residential course, led by specialists. They had a wave-tank where they could create extreme weather conditions - so we could get experience of what to do if the boat turned over in a storm at night, for example.
13:13DAVID: Since I started, I've had to deal with a range of emergency situations. But the work's hugely motivating. It's not just about saving lives - I've learned a lot about the technology involved. My background in IT's been useful here, and I can use my expertise to help other volunteers. They're a great group - we're like a family really, which helps when you're dragging yourself out of bed on a cold stormy night. But actually, it's the colder months that can be the most rewarding time. That's when the incidents tend to be more serious, and you realise that you can make a huge difference to the outcome. So if any of you listeners are interested...
14:04ANNOUNCER: That is the end of Part 2. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 2.

groups.title: Questions 17 and 18
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO things does David say about the lifeboat volunteer training?

groups.title: Questions 19 and 20
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO things does David find most motivating about the work he does?

q11.text: What made David leave London and move to Northsea?
options: A. He was eager to develop a hobby.
B. He wanted to work shorter hours.
C. He found his job in website design unsatisfying.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (He was eager to develop a hobby)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'keen on boats as a teenager... pursue that interest a bit more in my free time.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'pursue that interest in my free time' = develop a hobby.

q12.text: The Lifeboat Institution in Northsea was built with money provided by
options: A. a local organisation.
B. a local resident.
C. the local council.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (a local resident)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'funds provided by a generous member of the public who'd lived here all her life.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'member of the public who'd lived here' = local resident.

q13.text: In his health assessment, the doctor was concerned about the fact that David
options: A. might be colour blind.
B. was rather short-sighted.
C. had undergone eye surgery.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (might be colour blind)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'They gave me tests for colour blindness and they thought I might have a problem there...'
• Phân tích bẫy: David từng cận thị và đã mổ laser ('had laser eye surgery... so that was OK'), bác sĩ lo lắng về việc mù màu (colour blindness).

q14.text: After arriving at the lifeboat station, they aim to launch the boat within
options: A. five minutes.
B. six to eight minutes.
C. eight and a half minutes.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (six to eight minutes)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'then we try to get the boat off the dock and out to sea in another six to eight minutes.'
• Phân tích bẫy: 5 phút là thời gian có mặt tại trạm ('get there in five minutes'); 8 phút rưỡi là mức trung bình toàn quốc ('average time across the country's eight and a half minutes').

q15.text: As a 'helmsman', David has the responsibility of deciding
options: A. who will be the members of his crew.
B. what equipment it will be necessary to take.
C. if the lifeboat should be launched.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (if the lifeboat should be launched)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'it's ultimately my decision whether it's safe to launch the boat.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'decision whether it's safe to launch' = deciding if the lifeboat should be launched.

q16.text: As well as going out on the lifeboat, David
options: A. gives talks on safety at sea.
B. helps with fundraising.
C. recruits new volunteers.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (gives talks on safety at sea)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I speak to youth groups and sailing clubs in the area about the sorts of problems that sailors and swimmers can have...'
• Phân tích bẫy: Việc gây quỹ (fundraising) là do các tình nguyện viên khác làm ('other volunteers who organise activities to raise money for us').

q17.text: Which TWO things does David say about the lifeboat volunteer training? (Ý 1)
options: A. The residential course developed his leadership skills.
B. The training in use of ropes and knots was quite brief.
C. The training exercises have built up his mental strength.
D. The casualty care activities were particularly challenging for him.
E. The wave tank activities provided practice in survival techniques.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (The training exercises have built up his mental strength)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'it's given me the confidence to deal with extreme situations without panicking.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'confidence to deal with extreme situations without panicking' = built up mental strength.

q18.text: Which TWO things does David say about the lifeboat volunteer training? (Ý 2)
options: A. The residential course developed his leadership skills.
B. The training in use of ropes and knots was quite brief.
C. The training exercises have built up his mental strength.
D. The casualty care activities were particularly challenging for him.
E. The wave tank activities provided practice in survival techniques.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: E (The wave tank activities provided practice in survival techniques)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'They had a wave-tank where they could create extreme weather conditions - so we could get experience of what to do if the boat turned over in a storm at night...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'what to do if the boat turned over in a storm' = survival techniques.

q19.text: Which TWO things does David find most motivating about the work he does? (Ý 1)
options: A. working as part of a team
B. experiences when working in winter
C. being thanked by those he has helped
D. the fact that it keeps him fit
E. the chance to develop new equipment

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (working as part of a team)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'They're a great group - we're like a family really, which helps when you're dragging yourself out of bed...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'great group - like a family' = working as part of a team.

q20.text: Which TWO things does David find most motivating about the work he does? (Ý 2)
options: A. working as part of a team
B. experiences when working in winter
C. being thanked by those he has helped
D. the fact that it keeps him fit
E. the chance to develop new equipment

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (experiences when working in winter)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'it's the colder months that can be the most rewarding time. That's when the incidents tend to be more serious...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'colder months' = winter; 'most rewarding' = most motivating.
